subject: SOC2 packet shared — any blockers on review / quick check-in
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@solstice-analytics.com>; Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@solstice-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + SOC2 packet for Solstice Analytics — next steps
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_packet_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 1.4MB)

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — good call. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so legal & security can keep moving: 

- What we covered: architecture overview, data flows for inference (no persistent storage of PII in our control plane), and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated).
- Action items I noted for Solstice: 1) Share SOC 2 package with legal/security, 2) Confirm data retention policy needs for logs, 3) Decide whether on-prem or VPC Private deployment is required for pilot.

I attached our SOC2 packet (reports + sysdesc) and a small sample of the logs export format so your team can validate retention/formatting.

Proposed next steps:
- Your legal/security review and any blocker items (expected by mid-next week?)
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min follow-up with our security engineer to walk the packet line-by-line (here’s my calendar: https://calendly.com/dylan-redwood/30min).

If there’s anything I missed in the recap, please flag. I’ll follow up later this week if I don’t hear back.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0182 | dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

--
Redwood_SOC2_packet_v1.2.pdf — Contains: SOC2 Type II attestation (2025), control matrix, system architecture, change management logs.
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@solstice-analytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@solstice-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + SOC2 packet for Solstice Analytics — next steps

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the recap and the packet. I shared both with our legal and infra teams yesterday. A couple quick notes from my side: 

- Legal is looking at the SOC2 report now; they asked whether Redwood supports per-customer log retention rules (our logs team wants 90 days by default, but may need 365 days for certain data classes).
- Infra asked for a sample export of request logs (format/fields) — if you can point me to the specific schema or drop a tiny sample it’ll help speed review.

We’re planning to surface feedback by early next week unless anything shows up sooner.

—Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Legal & Compliance | Solstice Analytics
aisha@solstice-analytics.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@solstice-analytics.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@solstice-analytics.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Checking in — any blockers on SOC2 review / prioritization?

Hi Aisha — bumping to check whether anything is blocking the review. Two quick notes that may help your teams: 

- Per-customer retention: we support configurable retention policies at the account level; default exports include timestamps, request_id, model, prompt_hash, response_size. See attached sample (redwood-logs-sample-2026-02.txt).
- If it helps, I can have our infra/security engineer join and walk your team through fields and redaction options (I’ve cc’d Stephanie from our security team).

Also trying to get a sense of timing and priority on your side so we can plan pilot capacity. If the legal review will take more than two weeks, we can set a tentative pilot window and adjust if needed.

If easier, here’s my calendar: https://calendly.com/dylan-redwood/30min — feel free to grab a slot that works for you.

Thanks — appreciate it.
Dylan
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@solstice-analytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha@solstice-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checking in — any blockers on SOC2 review / prioritization?

On Mon, Feb 27, 2026 at 11:30 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Aisha — bumping to check whether anything is blocking the review. Two quick notes that may help your teams: 
> 
> - Per-customer retention: we support configurable retention policies at the account level; default exports include timestamps, request_id, model, prompt_hash, response_size. See attached sample (redwood-logs-sample-2026-02.txt).

Thanks for the follow-up, Dylan. We’re still in legal review — thing that came up is whether request-level metadata (prompt_hash) is considered a derivative that would need special handling. They asked for a short note on how you derive hashes and whether they’re reversible. Also, can you confirm whether the logs export contains any short-lived tokens or keys?

If you can send a 1-paragraph description we can share with counsel and I’ll try to get back with a decision on timing later this week.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
CTO | Solstice Analytics
tom.reynolds@solstice-analytics.com

redwood-logs-sample-2026-02.txt (attachment referenced): lines show example fields and formats — timestamps ISO8601, request_id (uuid), model_id, prompt_hash (sha256), response_size_bytes
